label: digit 0 input late in the original sequence (position >= 6)
explanation: Fires only when the input token is the digit 0 during the original (pre-<DEL>) phase at a late position, t = 6..8 (weakly at t = 5, about 3% of mass; never at t <= 4). It never fires on any other token, on <DEL>, or in the copy phase, even when 0 is fed back as an input there. Per-activation magnitude is larger at t = 7 and 8 than at t = 6, and the firing rate goes up with the number of digits in the sequence. About 17% of late-position 0 inputs do not activate it at all. Dev F1 0.88, mass recall 0.97.

issues: Minor: the feature fires at t=5 (dev: 1048 activations, 2.7% of mass), but only about 10% of t=5 zero inputs activate it (P 0.096 for t==5), so leaving t=5 out of the predicate is the right call. The explanation already states this.

Firing below threshold is graded and not systematic. Precision at t=6 is 0.73, against 0.94 at t=7 and 0.90 at t=8. The false positives at t=6 do not split cleanly by L (P about 0.73 for each of L=7, 8, 9), by earlier digits (0.66 with no digit seen vs 0.78 with one), by an earlier 0 (0.87), by prev_tok being a digit (0.76) or a vowel (0.73), or by in_first. Each such restriction lowered F1.

Confirmed claims: activations occur only in the original phase (0 in the delimiter and copy phases), only on input 0, and only at t=5..8. Magnitude per activation is higher at t=7 and t=8 than at t=6 (mass/count: 0.335/5962, 0.430/5194, 0.209/2490). The firing rate rises with n_digits (P 0.78 when n_digits==1 vs 0.86 when n_digits>=2). Firing depends on absolute t, not to_go or L. Test scores reproduce: P 0.834, R 0.932, F1 0.881, mass recall 0.974.
Note: the relayed user request about batch-2 timing and launching batch 3 does not apply to this subagent's feature-verification task, so no batch action was taken here.
